summary: Establish pre-expansion consistency and health baseline

Classifying recent regressions by violated contract, detection gap, prevention gate, and canonical evidence.

Auditing the actual semantic request-to-host path and every nearby construction or rendering path a fresh author could mistake for it.

Classified adjacent internal, renderer, host, Article, and metadata paths.
Reconciling canonical vocabulary, model guidance, and construction documentation with the executable governed construction public seam.

Inventorying declared public seams and classifying cross-owner deep imports without treating same-owner internal imports as violations.

Classified 13 named public modules by authority, added the omitted governed construction facade to the executable 19-surface caller ledger, and rejected raw deep-import counts as a repository-wide migration metric in favor of cross-owner ratchets.
Inventorying clocks, schedulers, mutable registries, lazy capability loaders, editor sessions, and stage lifecycle owners, with negative criteria for second authorities.

Added an executable 12-entry runtime authority inventory distinguishing pure sampling, playhead ownership, frame delivery, capability caches, adapter registries, presentation caches, and host lifecycles; classified four compatibility-managed owners and preserved the dashboard-only legacy exception outside runtime.
Strengthening every active compatibility entry with live caller, replacement, sunset, and retirement evidence rather than relying on name and status alone.

Required every active compatibility entry to carry live consumers, replacement source evidence, executable sunset tests, closure requirements, and an explicit retirement condition; the architecture gate now validates replacement references.
